issues.description: Older equal-rank terminal records can overwrite newer terminal job state, end time, elapsed time, and exit code.
Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, so valid transient states can cause later RUNNING/PENDING updates to be skipped as stale.
Upsert marks rows unchanged using only state, end, and elapsed_sec, ignoring corrected user, partition, CPU, GPU, and exit_code fields.
Parser accepts negative AllocCPUS and negative GPU TRES values, allowing reports to show negative resource usage.
Parser accepts empty user and partition values even though the database schema and reports assume meaningful grouping keys.
Reference timestamps are stored and compared as raw ISO strings, which produces incorrect ordering/filtering when timezone offsets are present.
Newest reference time uses SQLite MAX over timestamp text, so top-user windows can be anchored to the wrong record with mixed offset-aware timestamps.
Ingest does not handle SQLite connection/write failures, so common filesystem or database errors surface as tracebacks instead of CLI errors.
Report commands do not handle missing, corrupt, locked, or unwritable SQLite databases and will crash with raw sqlite3 exceptions.
Schema has no versioning or migration path, making future active development risky once user databases exist.
No indexes support reference-time filtering or grouping, so reports will full-scan the jobs table as sacct history grows.
Project lacks configured linting, formatting, type checking, or coverage gates despite being a CLI that performs accounting calculations.
